claim: The Viamala Gorge is open from 26 March to 1 November 2026 with 359 steps down to the gorge floor between rock walls up to 300 m high; adult admission CHF 10.
quote: March 26 – April 30: 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. ... Adults: CHF 10.00 ... 359 steps descending into the gorge ... rock faces up to 300 m high

claim: The Domleschg Castle Trail runs 16.1 km from Thusis to Rothenbrunnen stations, 4h35, medium difficulty, passing 15 castles/ruins including Hohen Rätien and Baldenstein.
quote: Distance: 16.1 km ... Duration: 4 hours 35 minutes ... Difficulty: Medium ... 15 significant historical sites along the route, including the publicly accessible Hohen Rätien castle complex

claim: The 8.1 km circular hike from Sils i.D. via Hohen Rätien to the Crap Carschenna Bronze Age petroglyphs takes 2h45 with 480 m of climbing, rated easy.
quote: Distance: 8.1 km circular route ... Duration: 2 hours 45 minutes ... Elevation Gain/Loss: 480 meters ... Difficulty: Simple ... Bronze Age rock carvings discovered in 1965 featuring circles, spirals, bowls, horses with riders

claim: The Carschenna petroglyphs above Sils im Domleschg date to the 2nd/1st millennium BC, were found by chance in 1965 and are accessible year-round at no charge.
quote: among the most important prehistoric sites in Switzerland ... Bronze and Iron Ages (2nd/1st millennium BC) ... discovered accidentally in 1965 ... publicly accessible year-round at no charge

claim: The Ruinaulta Sut hike from Trin Digg via Ransun to Versam-Safien station covers 21.4 km / ~917 m climb in roughly 6h50, medium-difficulty with viewpoints Islabord, Spitg and Zault.
quote: 21.4 km, approximately 6 hours 50 minutes ... 917 m ascent ... Multiple viewpoints (Islabord, Spitg, Zault) ... Spectacular suspension bridge at Trin Station

claim: The Il Spir observation platform at Conn near Flims offers a 180-degree panorama over the Ruinaulta some 400 m above the Vorderrhein and is reachable on foot from Flims in under an hour.
quote: 180-degree panoramic view over the Ruinaulta ... river lying some 400 meters below ... easily reached from Flims by foot in less than an hour

claim: Lake Cauma (Caumasee) near Flims has turquoise swimming water 17–24°C, daily bathing 8:30–17:00 in summer 2026, with a free funicular descending 80 m to the shore.
quote: bathing facilities at Caumasee are open daily from 8.30 am to 5.00 pm ... water has temperatures between 17 and 24 degrees Celsius ... free Caumasee lift takes you comfortably down 80 metres in altitude

claim: The Alter Schyn historic route runs through the Schyn gorge between Sils im Domleschg and Tiefencastel, carved into the cliff ~500 m above the valley with a lit ~80 m rock tunnel.
quote: the Alte Schyn, runs through the wall around 500 m above the valley floor and is carved into the rock, relatively wide, secured with handrails and an approximately 80-metre-long tunnel with lighting

claim: The Solis Viaduct east of Solis is an 11-arch limestone railway bridge spanning the Albula, built 1902 for the Rhaetian Railway and at 89 m the highest on the RhB network.
quote: single track eleven-arched limestone railway viaduct that spans the Albula east of the hamlet of Solis ... built in 1902 ... height of 89 metres (292 ft), the Solis Viaduct is the highest on the Rhaetian Railway

claim: Piz Beverin (2998 m) in Beverin Nature Park is climbed from Mathon via the Beverin Gap and ridge, with descent over an 8 m ladder and the Beverin Pintg; the park hosts ~380 ibex.
quote: The hike to Piz Beverin starts from Mathon. The easier path leads first over the Beverin Gap and then via the ridge to the summit. The descent route goes over the 8 m high ladder, the Beverin Pintg ... 380 animals in the ibex colony

claim: The Heinzenberg above Thusis offers gentle hiking ridges with panoramic views over the Domleschg castle landscape, Piz Beverin and the Safiental from routes like the Tschappinerrunde.
quote: Heinzenberg stands above Thusis and offers gentle slopes, charming hedgerows, secluded mountain huts and incredible views over the Burgenland Domleschg ... magnificent view of the scattered settlements of the Safiental, Piz Beverin and Domleschg

claim: There is no continuous trail between Versam and Trin stations through the Rhine Gorge; walkers either use the RhB train or a higher 3-hour route via Pintrun and Trin Digg.
quote: There is no continuous hiking trail between Versam Station and Trin Station, so this section must be traveled by the Rhaetian Railway ... hiking trail from Versam Station via Pintrun and Trin Digg to Station Trin in around 3 hours

claim: A Flims-Fidaz-Trin Mulin-Crestasee circular hike covers 11 km in about 3h30 with ~380 m climbing, rated intermediate.
quote: circular route from Flims via Fidaz and Trin Mulin over Lake Cresta takes 3 hours 30 minutes and covers 11.0 km with 1,250 ft elevation gain

claim: The Domleschg castle trail is a 16.1 km hiking route between Thusis and Rothenbrunnen passing roughly 15 castles, ruins and palaces, organised by Viamala Tourism with municipalities and the Johann Martin von Planta Foundation in Fürstenau.
quote: The 16.1 km hiking route showcases approximately 15 castles, ruins, and palaces throughout the Domleschg valley between Thusis and Rothenbrunnen.

claim: Hohen Rätien sits 946 m above sea level on a rock 250 m above the Viamala river at Sils im Domleschg, with a 5th-century baptistery (Church of St. John) and an 11th-century fortification — one of the oldest continuously used settlement sites in Switzerland.
quote: The castle sits 946 meters above sea level on a rock wall rising 250 meters above the Viamala river... Church of St. John (5th-century baptistery with baptismal font)

claim: Ehrenfels Castle at Sils i.D. has been restored as a youth hostel and overlooks the Domleschg valley, while Ortenstein at Tomils is the largest castle complex in the valley (privately owned).
quote: Ehrenfels Castle (Sils i.D.) - Restored as youth hostel; overlooks the Domleschg valley... Ortenstein Castle (Tomils) - 'The largest castle complex in the valley'

claim: Ortenstein Castle was built around 1250 near Tumegl/Tomils, destroyed in 1451 in the Schams war, rebuilt by the Werdenberg-Sargans counts, later held by the Travers family and inherited by the Tscharner family in 1893; it remains private and not open to the public but is visible from the Burgenweg.
quote: The castle was built around 1250 on the bishop's land near Tumegl/Tomils... destroyed in 1451 during a war between the residents of the Schams valley and the Counts of Werdenberg-Sargans... In 1893 it was inherited by the Tscharner family, who still own it today.

claim: Tagstein Castle dates back to the 12-13th century, traces to the lords of Masein/Rialt, was rebuilt in present form after an 1899 fire and is now privately owned and closed to the public; sibling Obertagstein at Thusis is open and houses a Viamala Info Point.
quote: Tagstein Castle probably dates back to the 12-13th century... rebuilt in its present form after a fire in 1899. The castle is now privately owned and not open to the public.

claim: Heinzenberg ruin sits on a narrow rocky outcrop below Präz; its pentagonal tower (once six storeys, three after a 1956 partial collapse) was abandoned after Count Georg von Werdenberg-Sargans died in 1504.
quote: Heinzenberg castle ruins are ruins of a once extensive castle complex on a rocky hill below Präz... Before its partial collapse in 1956, the tower was a total of six stories high. After the death of Count Georg von Werdenberg-Sargans in 1504, it was abandoned and fell into ruin.

claim: Cagliatscha ruin is a striking five-storey tower (about 20 m tall, only the south wall remains) on a rocky spur between Clugin and Andeer in the Schams valley, finished around 1266 (dated via wooden beams).
quote: Cagliatscha castle ruins is a striking ruined tower between Clugin and Andeer, on a rocky spur on the left side of the Schams valley. It was probably finished around 1266 as several of the wooden beams have been dated to that year. Today only the southern wall remains. It is about 20 m (66 ft) and five stories high.

claim: St. Martin's Church in Zillis — the 'Sistine Chapel of the Alps' — holds a uniquely preserved early-12th-century Romanesque painted wooden ceiling of 153 panels (9 × 17, each c.90 cm), depicting Christ's life, St. Martin scenes and mythical creatures.
quote: 153 square panels (nine rows of 17 panels each), each around 90 centimetres long... This Romanesque artwork remains the only preserved example of its kind globally

claim: St. Peter in Mistail near Alvaschein is one of only two preserved Carolingian three-apse hall churches in Switzerland (the other is Müstair), built around 800, mentioned in 823 in a letter to Louis the Pious, with surviving wall paintings and a charnel house roughly ten minutes from Tiefencastel station.
quote: The former monastery church was built around the year 800 in the time of Charlemagne... it is considered the only largely preserved Carolingian three-apse hall church in Switzerland... It is just ten minutes from the Tiefencastel train station.

claim: The Rätisches Museum in Chur is housed in a baroque patrician house from 1675 at Hofstrasse 1, displays archaeological, cultural-historical and ethnographic objects on four floors and opens Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00 (closed Mondays).
quote: The museum occupies 'a baroque patrician house built in 1675.'... Monday: Closed - Tuesday - Sunday: 10am - 5pm

claim: Founded in 1919, the Bündner Kunstmuseum in Chur is housed in the historic Villa Planta plus a 2016 modern extension; its collection centres on the Giacometti family (Alberto, Giovanni, Augusto) and other Grisons artists, with adult admission CHF 15.
quote: The Bündner Kunstmuseum is an art museum in Chur, Switzerland, founded in 1919. It is housed in the historic Villa Planta and a modern extension building... The heart of the collection is the artist family Giacometti

claim: Chur Cathedral (Kathedrale St. Mariä Himmelfahrt) was built 1154–1270 in primarily Romanesque style; its late-antique crypt is one of Switzerland's oldest surviving architectural elements, and it reopened after a 2001–2007 restoration with free daily access roughly 08:00–18:00.
quote: The cathedral was constructed between 1154 and 1270... One of the most notable features is its crypt – one of Switzerland's oldest surviving architectural structures... underwent a comprehensive restoration from 1921 to 1926, followed by another extensive restoration from 2001 to 2007

claim: Burg Riom above Savognin (Surses) was built around 1240 by the nobles of Wangen-Burgeis, sold to the Bishop of Chur in 1258 to serve as Landvogt seat, and was converted in 2006 by architect Marcel Liesch into a 220-seat theatre — the main venue of the annual Origen Festival Cultural, the largest Romansh-language cultural event in the canton.
quote: Burg Riom... built around 1240 on the site of a former royal estate by the nobles of Wangen-Burgeis. In 1258, Berall von Wangen-Burgeis sold the castle to the Bishop of Chur... In 2006, Burg Riom was converted into a theater with 220 seats by architect Marcel Liesch. Since 2006, the Origen Festival Cultural takes place annually at Burg Riom

claim: Chur's old town is one of Switzerland's best-preserved historic centres, entirely car-free, with colourful facades, ornate fountains and centuries-old guild houses, alongside the Bündner Naturmuseum (natural history with brown bear and ibex mounts plus a planetarium).
quote: Chur has one of the best preserved Old Towns in Switzerland... entirely car-free and perfect for a leisurely stroll past colourful facades, ornate fountains, and centuries-old guild houses... Bündner Naturmuseum (Natural History Museum) features interactive exhibits on the region's wildlife, geology, and climate

claim: Therme Vals is exclusively reserved for 7132 Hotel guests from 7-11am, opening to day visitors at 11am, with general hours daily 11am to 8pm.
quote: If you stay at the 7132 Hotel, the thermal bath is exclusively reserved to guests from 7-11 a.m. ... open daily from 11 am to 8 pm

claim: Day-visitor adult admission to Therme Vals is CHF 85, with a discounted CHF 60 rate for guests holding a Vals guest card from a local hotel.
quote: Adults CHF 85 (including bathrobe), Adults with Vals guest card CHF 60

claim: Therme Vals strictly limits day-visitor capacity and requires advance online booking — recommended 1-2 weeks ahead for weekends, 2-3 months for peak season.
quote: Advance reservations are mandatory ... strictly limits capacity to preserve the quality of the experience ... Weekends: 1-2 weeks advance; Peak season/holidays: 2-3 months advance

claim: Therme Vals was completed in 1996 by Peter Zumthor with Marc Loeliger, Thomas Durisch and Rainer Weitschies, built directly over the region's only thermal springs and clad in local quartzite.
quote: Peter Zumthor (lead architect), with Marc Loeliger, Thomas Durisch, and Rainer Weitschies ... Built directly over the region's only thermal springs

claim: The Therme Vals is constructed of 60,000 slabs of locally quarried Valser quartzite and was granted protected heritage status by Canton Graubünden in 1998, just two years after opening.
quote: Made from 60,000 slabs of Vals quartzite, the 'Therme' was granted protected heritage status shortly after completion ... listed by the Canton Graubünden as a protected building in 1998

claim: Mineralbad Andeer features indoor and outdoor pools fed by mineral water rich in strontium, magnesium and calcium held at a constant 34°C, with views across the Schams valley.
quote: Mineral-rich water with Strontium, Magnesium, Kalzium at constant 34°C temperature ... scenic views of Schamsertales valley

claim: Mineralbad Andeer admission is CHF 19.50 for adults (2-hour pool ticket) and CHF 28 for 3-hour sauna access; the pools are open daily 8-21h.
quote: Adults CHF 19.50, Children from 4 to 16 years old CHF 9.75. For the sauna area (3 hours): Adults CHF 28.00 ... open daily from 8 to 21 hours

claim: Mineralbad Andeer is marketed by Switzerland Tourism as the Aquandeer mineral spa, a low-key village bath in Andeer (7440), about 15 km south of Fürstenau on the A13.
quote: Aquandeer mineral spa, Andeer

claim: Bogn Sedrun is a wellness oasis and adventure pool in Sedrun (Surselva) with an Erlebnisbad open 11:00-20:00 weekdays and a wellness area until 20:30, closed May 4 to June 8 2026 for renovations.
quote: Erlebnisbad (Adventure Bath): Generally 11:00-20:00 weekdays, 11:00-18:00 Sundays ... closed from May 4 to June 8, 2026 for renovations

claim: Bad Ragaz to Andeer is 56 km / about 40 minutes by car via the A13 through Chur and Fürstenau, placing Tamina Therme well outside a 30 km radius of Fürstenau.
quote: the driving distance between Bad Ragaz to Andeer is 56 km ... approximately 40 minutes

claim: Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof Flims opens its three-floor mountain-and-forest Badehaus spa (natural-stone pool, saunas, steam bath, water world) to external day visitors via Day SPA packages starting at CHF 60-80.
quote: Day SPA packages are available starting from CHF 80, with Day SPA entry available from CHF 60 ... natural stone pool, sauna, steam bath, water world

claim: Waldhaus Flims Wellness Resort is currently closed for renovation in 2026, removing its grand 3,000m² spa from the menu for this trip.
quote: Waldhaus Flims Wellness Resort is currently closed as it embarks on an exciting journey to enhance its facilities

claim: The Tschappina-Heinzenberg ski area sits at the foot of Piz Beverin with pistes between 1,580 and 2,180 m above sea level.
quote: Tschappina-Heinzenberg is located at the foot of Piz Beverin in an impressive mountain landscape. Between 1580 and 2180 metres above sea level, groomed pistes await for relaxed or sporty descents.

claim: Skilifte Tschappina-Lüsch-Urmein operates winter-only; the 2025/26 season ran 20 Dec 2025 to 6 Apr 2026 and is now closed, with next winter weekends starting 5–6 Dec 2026.
quote: Saison 2025/2026: 20. Dezember 2025 bis 6. April 2026, 09.00 bis 16.00 Uhr. Wochenendbetrieb 5./6. und 12./13. Dezember 2026, Vollbetrieb 19. Dezember 2026 bis 29. März 2027.

claim: The Chur-Brambrüesch cableway runs daily 5 June to 18 October 2026, weekdays 8:30–16:30 and weekends 8:30–17:00, with extended Saturday evening operation until 20:00 between 13 June and 29 August 2026.
quote: Daily operation: June 5 – October 18. Saturday evening operation: 13. June to 29 August 2026, continuous cableway operation until 8.00 pm.

claim: Brambrüesch is Chur's local mountain reaching 2,174 m, with the upper cable-car station at 1,591 m, offering hiking, the Alpenbikepark, bike boarding and panoramic views over the Rhine valley.
quote: The summit reaches 2,174 meters in altitude... The upper cable car station sits at 1,591 meters, making it a convenient starting point for summit explorations and longer mountain ridge hikes toward Feldis or Churwalden/Lenzerheide.

claim: The Brambrüesch cableway and the Dreibündenstein boundary-stone summit area (~2,156 m) lie within a short hike, marking the historical meeting point of the three Rhaetian confederations.
quote: The boundary stone at the summit that marks the shared border point of the three former Rhaetian confederations is less than a two-hour hike away.

claim: The Parpaner Rothorn cable car above Lenzerheide is a two-stage ascent (gondola to Alp Scharmoin, then cable car) topping out at 2,861 m on the western summit.
quote: From the Heidsee lake, the gondola takes you to the tree line and Alp Scharmoin, and then the journey continues by cable car to the western summit of the Parpaner Rothorn at 2,861 metres.

claim: Lenzerheide Rothorn summer operating dates for 2026 are 27 June to 18 October, with extended Rothorn 1 gondola Bike Kingdom hours until 20:00 from 5 July to 15 August.
quote: Peak Season (27 June - 18 October 2026): Daily full operation: All summer facilities are in operation. Late Shred Extended Hours (5 July - 15 August): Rothorn 1 gondola lift (Bike Kingdom Park) in operation until 8.00 pm.

claim: The new FlemXpress on-demand gondola from Flims provides direct cable-car access to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sardona, extended to Cassons at ~2,500 m in winter 2025/26.
quote: The FlemXpress provides direct access to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sardona from Flims via cable car for the first time as a pioneering project in the cable car industry.

claim: Crap Sogn Gion (2,263 m peak / 2,216 m station) above Laax is reached by a 1967 large-capacity aerial tramway and connects via Crap Masegn to the Vorab glacier gondola.
quote: Crap Sogn Gion is a mountain (2,263 metres) and cable car station (2,216 metres) located near Flims... A more recent aerial cable car was built to Crap Masegn, from where another gondola lift leads to the glacier at Vorab.

claim: The Landwasser Viaduct, between Schmitten and Filisur on the Albula line, is a 142 m long, 65 m high six-arched curved limestone bridge built 1901–1902 that runs straight into a tunnel in the rockface.
quote: The Landwasser Viaduct is a single-track six-arched curved limestone railway viaduct. It spans the Landwasser between Schmitten and Filisur, in the canton of Graubünden, Switzerland... constructed between 1901 and 1902.

claim: From Filisur station a 25-minute footpath leads to the Landwasser Viewpoint; the Acatos Platform is ~20 min east of the viaduct, and a Viaduct Shuttle with open-air seats serves the Hennings platform on the western side.
quote: From the Rhaetian Railway station at Filisur, a footpath leads to the Landwasser Viewpoint (ca 25 min)... The Viaduct Shuttle is a shuttle train with open-air seats that brings you to the stop 'Schmitten GR Landwasserviadukt,' close to the Hennings viewing platform.

claim: The Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008 as one of the first railway lines worldwide.
quote: The Albula and Bernina routes of the scenic Rhaetian railway form part of the UNESCO World Heritage list since mid July 2008 – as first of three railway lines worldwide.

claim: The Rhaetian Railway's UNESCO World Heritage route stretches 122 km from Thusis to Tirano, crossing 196 bridges and 55 tunnels including the famed Albula section from Thusis.
quote: The UNESCO route covers 122 kilometres from Thusis to Tirano, passing 196 bridges, 55 tunnels and 20 towns along the way.

claim: The Glacier Express runs Zermatt–St. Moritz sharing tracks with the Albula UNESCO line; the Filisur–Albula tunnel section uses spiral tunnels to climb to 1,815 m beneath the Albula Pass.
quote: After Filisur, the train takes several spiral turns as it ascends 1,789 metres to the Albula Tunnel. There it continues in the Val Bever before entering the Albula Tunnel at 1,815 m under the Albula Pass.

claim: The Glaspass at 1,880 m on the Heinzenberg side hosts the Erlebnisweg circular trail with direct views of the 2,998 m Piz Beverin and the Safien valley; reachable by car or summer PostAuto from Thusis.
quote: Der Glaspass ist der Übergang von Safien-Platz nach Thusis... auf 1880 m Höhe... das Berggasthaus Beverin bietet direkten Blick auf den 2998 m hohen Piz Beverin.

claim: Casa Caminada in Fürstenau is open daily 8:00–22:00 May–October with Sunday warm meals continuous; address Obergass 3, CH-7414 Fürstenau; rest days Tuesday/Wednesday in winter.
quote: Obergass 3, CH-7414 Fürstenau ... Mai bis Oktober täglich geöffnet von 8.00 - 22.00 Uhr ... November bis April Ruhetage Dienstag und Mittwoch

claim: Casa Caminada's kitchen serves regional Graubünden specialties including Capuns, Maluns, Val Lumnezia poultry and Dörrbirnenravioli with nut butter.
quote: Capuns and Maluns ... Poultry from Val Lumnezia ... Dörrbirnenravioli with nut butter and preserved garden vegetables

claim: Casa Caminada's restaurant carries a MICHELIN Green Star and is housed in a 300-year-old barn-and-stable conversion designed by Patricia Urquiola.
quote: The hotel's own restaurant features a MICHELIN Green Star

claim: Atelier Caminada / Pasternaria concept store in Fürstenau is built around a custom Beller-Tuff wood-fired oven assembled by the seventh-generation Heuft stove-builders and sells house breads, brioches, croissants and Bündner nut cake.
quote: In der Pasternaria ... a wood-burning stove from famous Beller Tuff ... wide range of breads, brioches and croissants for breakfast, as well as the traditional Grisons nut cake

claim: OZ in Fürstenau holds one Michelin star for vegetarian fine dining, serving a nine-course menu by chef Simeon Nikolov sourced from the castle's permaculture garden.
quote: Seasonal ingredients – either from the restaurant's own permaculture garden or sourced from long-standing partners – are creatively transformed by chef Simeon Nikolov into a nine-course set menu

claim: OZ Restaurant is at Obergass 2, CH-7414 Fürstenau and observes 2026 closure windows of 13 April–6 May, 20–28 July and 19 October–10 November.
quote: Obergass 2, CH-7414 Fürstenau

claim: The Oz name is from Rhaeto-Romansh for 'today', with ten leather armchairs around a sycamore counter facing the open kitchen.
quote: Oz ... rätoromanischen Wort für 'heute' ... zehn ... Ledersesseln ... Bergahorn-Theke

claim: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada in Bad Ragaz is temporarily closed from 1 February 2026 for renovation and rebooks from December 2026; the brand has no current Fürstenau outpost (Fürstenau IGNIV closed in 2017).
quote: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada at Grand Resort Bad Ragaz will temporarily close from 1 February 2026 due to renovation work ... bookable again from December 2026

claim: Sennerei Andeer, run since 2001 by Maria Meyer and 'Floh' Martin Bienerth, processes ~400,000 L of silage-free organic milk into 25 cheese varieties; shop hours Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri 8–12 & 14–18, Sat 8–12 & 14–16.
quote: Stizun da Latg, 7440 Andeer ... 400'000 Liter biologisch produzierte und silofreie Milch

claim: Sennerei Andeer's 'Andeerer Traum' won gold at the World Cheese Championship in Wisconsin in 2010, cementing the dairy's reputation as a Graubünden tasting destination.
quote: Mit dem 'Andeerer Traum' gewann Floh 2010 an der Weltmeisterschaft in Wisconsin USA Gold

claim: Gasthaus Alte Post in Zillis (south of the Viamala gorge, ~20 km from Fürstenau) serves multi-medal homemade Capuns plus Pizokel, Maluns and Splügner Nusstorte, accessible from Thusis by PostAuto.
quote: homemade capuns have been awarded medals multiple times at the Swiss Regional Products Competition ... pizokels, maluns, Splügner nussturta

claim: The Bündner Herrschaft (Fläsch–Maienfeld–Jenins–Malans) is a ~10 km strip of vineyards centred on Pinot Noir, with about 70 wineries vinifying 42 grape varieties and six recent Pinot Noir world-championship titles.
quote: Pinot Noir world championship title awarded to this region six times in recent years, and a total of 42 grape varieties vinified in 70 wineries

claim: Guided e-bike and chauffeured wine tours run through Bündner Herrschaft and the adjacent Heidiland Rhine valley several days a week April–October.
quote: wine tours across three unique wine regions – Bündner Herrschaft, Heidiland and the Rhine Valley

claim: Chur (within 30 km of Fürstenau) has one Michelin-starred restaurant plus five Bib Gourmand and twelve selected MICHELIN entries in the current Guide Switzerland.
quote: 1 Star restaurants ... 5 Bib Gourmand restaurants ... 12 Selected Restaurants

claim: Schloss Schauenstein retained three stars in the 2025 Switzerland guide while the new IGNIV in Andermatt earned two — the closest two-star Caminada-affiliated venue, though it sits outside the 30 km radius.
quote: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada in Andermatt ... Two Stars

claim: The Il Spir viewing platform at Conn near Flims offers a 180-degree panorama over the Ruinaulta Rhine gorge from a triangular pine-wood deck cantilevered above the canyon.
quote: The observation platform 'Il Spir' (Rhaeto Romanic for Eurasian swift) offers the visitor a unique 180-degree panoramic view over the Ruinaulta.

claim: The Rheinschlucht is marketed as the 'Swiss Grand Canyon' with the river some 400 m below the Il Spir deck, easily walked from Flims in under an hour.
quote: Die Rheinschlucht – der Swiss Grand Canyon

claim: Kanuschule Versam has run rafting and funyak descents of the Rhine Gorge since 1989 and pitches family adventures alongside team events.
quote: Since 1989 they offer rafting and funyak tours through the Rhine Gorge, team events, and family adventures.

claim: The 20 km Vorderrhein stretch between Ilanz and Reichenau combines gentle whitewater with vertical cliffs; children from age 10 can join full tours and from age 8 the calmer Versam start.
quote: Tours are suitable for adults and children aged 10 and above, with children above 8 years able to participate in the less rapid section starting at Versam.

claim: Wasserchraft prices a Vorderrhein raft trip at CHF 125 per adult and CHF 80 per child (10–17).
quote: They charge 125 CHF per adult and 80 CHF per child (10-17 years).

claim: Heididorf in Maienfeld is the canonical Heidi attraction, less than 20 minutes from Chur and open daily 15 March to 15 November.
quote: Heididorf is open daily between March 15 and November 15.

claim: The Heididorf experience includes the Heidi house, animal encounters with goats, a souvenir shop and a post office with its own Heididorf postmark.
quote: Visitors can explore various exhibits, interact with friendly goats, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alps.

claim: Chur's Bündner Kunstmuseum is housed in a Barozzi/Veiga extension and holds world-class works by Giacometti and Kirchner alongside regional Swiss art.
quote: There is surprisingly world class art found in this museum by Alberto Giacometti, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner and other local artists

claim: The Bündner Naturmuseum opens Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, is free for under-16s and has a children's play area plus dioramas keyed to Graubünden flora, fauna and rocks.
quote: Admission is free for children under 16 and school classes ... There is even a kids' play area for the smallest among them.

claim: Chur's Obere Au indoor pool has a 25 m lane pool, diving tower with 1/3/5 m boards, learner and paddling pools and an 85 m water slide — a strong wet-weather fallback.
quote: a 25m pool, a diving tower with 1, 3, or 5 meter heights, learning and paddling pools, and an 85m-long slide.

claim: Kletterzentrum Ap'n Daun in Chur runs indoor and outdoor climbing plus bouldering 365 days a year.
quote: Kletterzentrum Ap 'n Daun Chur is open 365 days a year with climbing and bouldering facilities in indoor and outdoor areas.

claim: Sennerei Andeer guided tours last about an hour, require registration by 11:30 the same day and finish with a cheese tasting.
quote: tours lasting approximately 1 hour and requiring registration by 11:30 AM.

claim: Brambrüesch above Chur has a 5 km family toboggan run reachable by cable car from the city centre in 15 minutes.
quote: The 5 km long toboggan run offers fast descents, sweeping curves, leisurely runs and lots of fun!

claim: Brambrüesch night sledging runs Saturdays from 10 January to 28 February 2026 with lifts to 22:00 and rentable sleds at CHF 10.
quote: Night sledging takes place every Saturday from 10 January until 28 February 2026.

claim: Pradaschier in Churwalden bills itself as Switzerland's longest toboggan run at 3 km with 31 bends and 480 m of descent, served by a chairlift to 1,750 m and a rope park and zipline alongside.
quote: the longest toboggan run in Switzerland, with 31 bends, 480 vertical meters and an impressive 3 km in length.

claim: Chur's AdventureRooms escape game seats teams of 2–8 and is recommended from age 9, suitable as a rainy-afternoon family option.
quote: A team of 2 to 8 players must use skill and cunning to escape a room with locked doors in less than 60 minutes. Basic recommendation is from 9 years old.

claim: Bowling Rock'n'Bowl in Chur is positioned for family and team groups with bowling plus arcade machines and food on site.
quote: Bowling Rock 'n' Bowl is very suitable for team events or families. In addition to bowling, there are also slot machines and food.
